title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The king asks the daughters' hands for the Infantes (tirada 104, third part, lines 2068–2126)
part: Tirada 104 (third part) · The king asks the daughters' hands for the Infantes (lines 2068–2126)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 258–261, lines 2068–2126 (tiradas 104–104). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Al otro día mañana, assí commo salió el sol,
el obispo don Jero[me] la missa cantó.
sentences.l:
At-the other day morning, as-soon-as came-out the sun,
the bishop don Jero[me] the mass sang.
sentences.i: Next morning, as soon as the sun was up, Bishop Don Jerome sang the mass.
sentences.n: Tirada 104 continued (assonance ó) — the king asks the Çid for his daughters for the Infantes of Carrión; the Çid entrusts them to the king, who marries them; the meeting ends, with the Çid's gifts to those who take their leave; the king hands the Infantes over to the Çid (Pidal's rubric, the part of it that falls here: El rey pide al Cid sus hijas para los infantes.—El Cid confía sus hijas al rey y éste las casa.—Las vistas acaban. Regalos del Cid a los que se despiden.—El rey entrega los infantes al Cid). The tirada and its stressed ó at the line-end (sol, cantó, son, conpeçó) run on from the previous part, which ended at v. 2067 with the Çid's feast. Al otro día mañana, 'on the next day in the morning', the morning after the feast (Otro día mañana, without the article, at v. 2062). assí commo, 'as soon as'. Jero[me], Jerome, the Çid's bishop of Valencia; the me is Pidal's (in italics). la missa cantó: the object before the verb, the verb kept for the line-end and the assonance.

sentences.t:
Al salir de la missa todos juntados son;
non lo tardó el rey, la razón conpeçó:
sentences.l:
At-the going-out from the mass all gathered are;
not it delayed the king, the speech he-began:
sentences.i: As they came out from mass they all gathered together; the king lost no time, and began to speak:
sentences.n: Al salir, 'on going out', al + infinitive. juntados son, 'are gathered', ser with the participle; the present son between the preterites cantó, tardó, conpeçó: the epic tense-mixing. non lo tardó, 'he did not delay it' (compare non lo detardan, v. 1964). la razón, 'the speech, the matter'. conpeçó = comenzó (conpeçar, 'to begin').

sentences.i: “Hear me, my household knights, counts and lesser nobles! I wish to lay a request before my Çid the Campeador — and may Christ so ordain that it be to his good.
sentences.n: Oidme = oíd + me, imperative 2nd pl. with the pronoun fastened on (printed here without the accent of Oídme at v. 1360). Pidal's note: escuelas, 'mesnadas', v. 1360 (Oídme, escuelas, e toda la mi cort!): a lord's household troops, his sworn following, not 'schools' ('my household knights', as there); here las escuelas with the article, 'you, my retinues'. cue[m]des, 'counts' (cuende, the old form of conde), the m Pidal's (in italics), as cue[mdes] at v. 1980. ifançones, 'infanzones', nobles of a rank below the counts and great lords. Pidal's note: cometer, 'proponer', 'to propose', as acometer at v. 1375. cometer quiero, the infinitive before the verb that governs it. assí lo mande Cristus, 'so may Christ ordain it', the present subjunctive as a wish, as in the Çid's assí lo mande el Criador (v. 2055); Cristus is the Latin form of the name. a so pro, 'to his profit, advantage' (so = su).

sentences.t:
Vuestras fijas vos pido, don Elvira e doña Sol,
que las dedes por mugieres, a ifantes de Carrión.
Semejam el casamiento ondrado e con grant pro,
ellos vos las piden e mándovoslo yo.
sentences.l:
Your daughters of-you I-ask, don Elvira and doña Sol,
that them you-give for wives, to Infantes of Carrión.
Seems-to-me the marriage honoured and with great profit,
they of-you them ask and I-command-you-it I.
sentences.i: I ask you for your daughters, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol, that you give them as wives to the Infantes of Carrión. The match seems to me an honourable one and of great advantage; they ask you for them, and I command it of you.
sentences.n: vos pido, 'I ask of you', vos the person asked. don Elvira: so printed, don and not doña, here and at vv. 2088, 2097 (beside doña Sol); kept as printed, 'Doña Elvira' in the English. que las dedes, 'that you give them': dedes, present subjunctive of dar (= deis). por mugieres, 'as wives' (mugier = mujer). ifantes de Carrión, as usual without the article. Semejam = semeja + m(e), 'it seems to me', the pronoun squeezed to -m and glued on (the enclitic squeeze). ondrado, 'honourable, bringing honour'; con grant pro, 'with great advantage'. mándovoslo = mando + vos + lo, 'I command you it', two pronouns stacked on the verb, and yo said again at the end: the request is also an order.

sentences.i: On this side and on that, all who are here, my men and yours, let them join in the asking: give them to us, my Çid, so may the Creator help you!”
sentences.n: Pidal's note: Della e della parte, 'de una y otra parte', 'on the one side and the other' (v. 1965). quantos que aquí son, 'as many as are here', the que pleonastic. que sean rogadores, 'let them be petitioners', que + subjunctive as a command. Pidal's note: the rogador was the one who solemnly interceded and asked for the bride in marriage; he received the bride and was the go-between in handing over the authority over her that was conferred on the husband or suitor (compare vv. 2088, 2097–99, 2132–37). rogadores ends in -ores: the stressed ó counts for the assonance and the unstressed -es after it is disregarded (so mejores, v. 2085, ifançones, v. 2072). dándoslas, 'give them to us': dad + nos + las, with the d and n of dadnos changed round (dadnos > dandos). si vos vala el Criador, 'so may the Creator help you': si here means 'so', a formula of adjuration, not 'if'; vala, present subjunctive of valer, 'to help'.

sentences.t:
—“Non abría fijas de casar”, respuso el Campeador,
“ca non han grant hedad e de dias pequeñas son.
De grandes nuevas son ifantes de Carrión,
perteneçen pora mis fijas e aun pora mejores.
sentences.l:
—“Not I-would-have daughters to marry”, answered the Campeador,
“for not they-have great age and of days small they-are.
Of great renown are Infantes of Carrión,
they-belong for my daughters and even for better.
sentences.i: “I have no daughters of an age to marry,” the Campeador answered, “for they are not old, and are young in years. The Infantes of Carrión are men of great renown, fit for my daughters, and for better still.
sentences.n: Non abría fijas de casar, 'I would not have daughters for marrying': abría = habría, the conditional of aver, a courteous demurral; de casar, 'to be married'. respuso, preterite of responder. han, 'they have' (aver as a full verb); hedad = edad, with a written h-. Pidal's note to v. 2083: the Çid's daughters are still de días pequeñas, or de días chicos (v. 269), that is, niñas, 'little girls' (vv. 255, 371, 1569), or iffantes (v. 1279), at the opening of the poem's action, on the journey to Valencia, and now at their betrothal (he refers to his note to v. 2703). Pidal's note: nuevas, 'renombre, fama', 'renown' (vv. 1154, 2683): De grandes nuevas, 'of great renown'. perteneçen pora, 'they are fitting for' (pora = para). aun pora mejores, 'and even for better (women)': the Çid's modesty, and a compliment to the suitors.

sentences.t:
Hyo las engendré amas e criásteslas vos,
entre yo y ellas en vuestra merçed somos nos;
afellas en vuestra mano don Elvira e doña Sol,
dadlas a qui quisiéredes vos, ca yo pagado so.”
sentences.l:
I them begot both and raised-them you,
between I and they in your mercy are we;
behold-them in your hand don Elvira and doña Sol,
give-them to whom you-may-wish you, for I satisfied am.”
sentences.i: I begot them both, and you brought them up; they and I alike are yours to command. Here they are in your hand, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol: give them to whom you will, for I am content.”
sentences.n: Hyo = yo, with an h- spelling, as hya = ya. amas = ambas, 'both'. criásteslas = criastes + las, 'you brought them up', preterite 2nd pl. (= criasteis). Pidal's note: the king had brought up the Çid's daughters (he refers to p. 92 of his introduction). Pidal's note to v. 2087: 'tanto yo como ellas estamos a vuestro mandar', 'both I and they are at your command'. entre yo y ellas, 'between I and they', meaning 'I and they together' (y here, e elsewhere); en vuestra merçed, 'at your mercy, your disposal'. afellas = afe + las, 'behold them', the presentative afe with the pronoun glued on (as afelo, afevos). a qui = a quien. quisiéredes, future subjunctive 2nd pl. of querer: 'whomever you may wish'. pagado so, 'I am satisfied' (so = soy). Putting the daughters 'in the king's hand' is the act Pidal's note to v. 2080 compares with the rogador's: the king now holds the power to give them.

sentences.t: —“Graçias”, dixo el rey, “a vos e a tod esta cort.”
sentences.l: —“Thanks”, said the king, “to you and to all this court.”
sentences.i: “My thanks,” said the king, “to you and to all this court.”
sentences.n: tod = toda, its final vowel lost before esta. cort = corte, which carries the ó assonance.

sentences.i: At once the Infantes of Carrión rose; they go to kiss the hands of him who was born in a good hour, and they exchanged swords before King Alfonso.
sentences.n: Luego, 'at once, straightway' (not modern 'later'). iffantes with ff, ifantes elsewhere: the print's spellings kept. ban = van, 'they go', b for v; on the scan the first letter is broken, and it is read as b (v would give the same word). ban besar, ir + infinitive without a, 'go to kiss'. al que en ora buena naçió, the formula, 'him who was born in a good hour', the Çid. The preterites levantaron, camearon with the present ban between them: the tense-mixing. camearon = cambiaron (camear, 'to exchange'). Pidal's note: 'cambiaron las espadas', in sign of kinship; it was common to give one's arms as a pledge of friendship, and so when Edmund, king of England, and Cnut, king of Denmark, made an alliance at the conference of Olney, they exchanged clothing and arms in sign of a pact of friendship. antel = ante el, 'before the'.

sentences.t:
Fabló rey don Alfons commo tan buen señor:
“Graçias, Çid, commo tan bueno, e primero al Criador,
quem dades vuestras fijas pora ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
Spoke king don Alfons as so good lord:
“Thanks, Çid, as so good, and first to-the Creator,
that-me you-give your daughters for Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: King Alfonso spoke, like the good lord he was: “Thanks to you, Çid, good man that you are — and first to the Creator — for giving me your daughters for the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: Fabló = habló (initial f- for modern h-). commo tan buen señor, 'as (befits) so good a lord'; commo tan bueno, the same turn said of the Çid. rey don Alfons, without the article. e primero al Criador, 'and first to the Creator': thanks are due to God before the Çid. quem = que me, 'that to me', the pronoun squeezed to -m; dades, present 2nd pl. of dar (= dais).

sentences.t:
Daquí las prendo por mis manos don Elvira e doña Sol,
e dólas por veladas a ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
From-here them I-take by my hands don Elvira and doña Sol,
and I-give-them for veiled-ones to Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: Here and now I take Doña Elvira and Doña Sol into my own hands, and give them as wedded wives to the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: Daquí = de aquí, 'from here', from this moment. las prendo … don Elvira e doña Sol, the pronoun before the verb and the names after it. prendo, 'I take' (prender). por mis manos, 'by my own hands': the king now acts as the rogador of Pidal's note to v. 2080, which cites these lines; he receives the brides and hands them on. dólas = do + las, 'I give them' (do = doy). por veladas, 'as veiled ones', that is, as lawful wives: velar was to veil the couple at the nuptial blessing, and velada the wife so married (Pidal's note to v. 2138 glosses el velar as 'la ceremonia de las velaciones', the ceremony of the nuptial veiling). The wedding itself is to be held in Valencia (v. 2105).

sentences.t:
Yo las caso a vuestras fijas con vuestro amor,
al Criador plega que ayades ende sabor.
sentences.l:
I them marry, your daughters, with your love,
to-the Creator may-it-please that you-have thereof pleasure.
sentences.i: I marry your daughters with your good will; may it please the Creator that you have joy of it.
sentences.n: Yo las caso a vuestras fijas: the object said twice, las before the verb and a vuestras fijas after it. con vuestro amor, 'with your love', here the Çid's good will and consent to the king's act, not a lord's favour to his vassal (the house's 'favour'), hence 'good will' in the English; vuestro amor is masculine, where the Çid said vuestra amor at v. 2032. plega, present subjunctive of plazer, 'may it please'. ayades, present subjunctive 2nd pl. of aver; ende, 'of it, thence'; aver sabor, 'to take pleasure' (as avien sabor, v. 2041).

sentences.t:
Afellos en vuestras manos ifantes de Carrión,
ellos vayan convusco, ca d' aquén me torno yo.
sentences.l:
Behold-them in your hands Infantes of Carrión,
they may-go with-you, for from this-side myself I-turn I.
sentences.i: Here are the Infantes of Carrión in your hands; let them go with you, for from here I turn back.
sentences.n: Afellos = afe + los, 'behold them', as afellas at v. 2088: the Çid put his daughters in the king's hand, and the king now puts the Infantes in the Çid's. vayan, present subjunctive, 'let them go'. convusco, 'with you'. d' aquén, 'from this side' (aquén, 'on this side', the opposite of allén, 'beyond'): from here, the Tajo, the king goes back. me torno, present for what he is about to do.

sentences.t:
Trezientos marcos de plata en ayuda les do yo,
que metan en sus bodas o dó quisiéredes vos;
sentences.l:
Three-hundred marks of silver in aid to-them give I,
that they-may-put into their weddings or where you-may-wish you;
sentences.i: Three hundred marks of silver I give them in aid, to spend on their wedding or wherever you may wish;
sentences.n: marcos, 'marks', a weight of silver. Pidal's note to v. 2103: the lord owed his vassal an ayuda de costa, a contribution to the cost, for his wedding; so Ruy Velázquez, in the legend of the Infantes de Lara, complains that his lord the count of Castile did not perform this duty well: “me costaron mucho mis bodas, et el conde Garci Fernández non me ayudó y tan bien como yo cuidé et él deviera”, 'my wedding cost me much, and Count Garci Fernández did not help me there as well as I expected and as he ought'. les do yo, 'I give to them' (do = doy). Pidal's note: metan, 'empleen, gasten', 'spend, lay out'. bodas, 'wedding' (plural, as in modern bodas). dó, 'where' (= donde): the mark over the letters is read as an accent; it might be an apostrophe, d'o, which the sense does not favour. quisiéredes, future subjunctive of querer.

sentences.t:
pues fueren en vuestro poder en Valençia la mayor,
los yernos e las fijas todos vuestros fijos son:
lo que vos ploguiere, dellos fet, Campeador.”
sentences.l:
once they-shall-be in your power in Valençia the great,
the sons-in-law and the daughters all your children are:
what to-you may-please, of-them do, Campeador.”
sentences.i: once they are in your keeping in Valencia the great, sons-in-law and daughters alike are all your children: do with them as you please, Campeador.”
sentences.n: pues, 'once, since'. fueren, future subjunctive of seer, 'shall be'. en vuestro poder, 'in your power', under your authority. Valençia la mayor, 'Valencia the great', the city's standing epithet. yernos, 'sons-in-law'; fijos, 'sons', here 'children', the masculine plural covering both. ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer, 'whatever may please'. dellos = de ellos. fet, 'do!', imperative 2nd pl. of fer (= haced), the -d of the ending written -t.

sentences.t:
Mio Çid gelos reçibe, las manos le besó:
“Mucho vos lo gradesco, commo a rey e a señor!
Vos casades mis fijas, ca non gelas do yo.”
sentences.l:
My Çid them-from-him receives, the hands to-him he-kissed:
“Much to-you it I-thank, as to king and to lord!
You marry my daughters, for not them-to-them give I.”
sentences.i: My Çid receives them from him and kissed his hands: “I thank you greatly for it, as my king and my lord! It is you who marry my daughters, for it is not I who give them.”
sentences.n: gelos = ge + los, 'them from him': ge, the old dative pronoun (ancestor of modern se) before an object pronoun; los, the Infantes. reçibe, present, besó, preterite: the tense-mixing. gradesco = agradezco. commo a rey e a señor, 'as (one thanks) a king and lord'. Vos casades, 'you marry', with vos said and stressed; gelas = ge + las, 'them to them'. The Çid insists that the marriage is the king's act, not his; the next tirada turns on this (Pidal's rubric to tirada 105: El Cid no quiere entregar las hijas por sí mismo, 'the Cid will not hand over his daughters himself').

sentences.t:
Las palabras son puestas, [los omenajes dados son],
que otro dia mañana quando salie[sse] el sol,
ques tornasse cada uno don salidos son.
sentences.l:
The words are set, [the homages given are],
that other day morning when should-come-out the sun,
that-himself should-return each one where gone-out they-are.
sentences.i: The words are agreed and the pledges given: that next morning, when the sun rose, each should go back to where he had come from.
sentences.n: son puestas, 'are set', agreed (poner palabras, 'to fix terms'). [los omenajes dados son], the whole half-line Pidal's (in italics), with no note on this page. omenajes, 'homages', the solemn pledges given. que, 'that': what was agreed follows. otro dia mañana, 'next morning', dia printed without its accent here. salie[sse], imperfect subjunctive of salir, the sse Pidal's (in italics). The third line is numbered 2112b in the print. ques = que se; tornasse, imperfect subjunctive of tornar, 'return'. don = donde, 'where, whence'; salidos son, 'they have come out', the perfect of a verb of motion made with ser: each is to go home.

sentences.t: Aquís metió en nuevas mio Çid el Campeador;
sentences.l: Here-himself put into renown my Çid the Campeador;
sentences.i: Then my Çid the Campeador did a thing to be talked of:
sentences.n: Aquís = aquí + se, 'here (he) himself', aquí of time, 'then'. Pidal's note: Aquís metió en nuevas, 'entonces hizo cosa señalada', 'then he did a notable thing'; Pidal records that Bello understood 'he won fame and praise' and Hinard 'then he set about making largesses', and that the other translators follow one or the other. nuevas, 'renown, fame', as at v. 2084: he put himself in men's mouths. The semicolon leads into the list of gifts that follows.

sentences.t:
tanta gruessa mula e tanto palafré de sazón,
tantas buenas vestiduras que d' alfaya son,
conpeçó mio Çid a dar a quien quiere prender so don;
cada uno lo que pide, nadi nol dize de no.
sentences.l:
so-much stout mule and so-much palfrey of season,
so-many good garments that of value are,
began my Çid to give to whom wants to-take his gift;
each one what he-asks, nobody not-to-him says of no.
sentences.i: So many stout mules, so many palfreys in their prime, so many fine garments of great price my Çid began to give to whoever would take his gift; each man had what he asked for, and no one was told no.
sentences.n: Pidal prints v. 2116 before v. 2115 and keeps both numbers; we follow his print order (2114, 2116, 2115, 2117). In that order the three things given come first, and the verb conpeçó … a dar after them. tanta gruessa mula, tanto palafré, the singular after tanto for 'so many', as tanta mula preçiada at v. 1966. gruessa, 'stout, sturdy'. palafré, the riding horse for the road, not the war-horse. de sazón, 'in good condition, in its prime'. Pidal's note: d' alfaya, 'de valor', 'of value'. conpeçó … a dar, 'began to give' (conpeçar = comenzar). quiere, present among preterites. prender so don, 'to take his gift' (so = su). nadi = nadie; nol = non le, 'not to him'; dize de no, 'says no': nadi … nol, the double negative, the negatives adding up rather than cancelling.

sentences.t: Mio Çid de los cavallos sessaenta dio en don.
sentences.l: My Çid of the horses sixty gave in gift.
sentences.i: Of the horses, my Çid gave sixty as gifts.
sentences.n: de los cavallos, 'of the horses', partitive: of the war-horses (the mules and palfreys were named at v. 2114). sessaenta = sesenta. dio en don, 'gave as a gift'.

sentences.t:
Todos son pagados de las vistas quantos que y son;
partir se quieren, que entrada era la noch.
sentences.l:
All are satisfied with the meeting as-many-as that there are;
to-part themselves they-want, for entered was the night.
sentences.i: All who are there are well pleased with the meeting; they wish to go their ways, for night had fallen.
sentences.n: pagados, 'satisfied, pleased' (pagado so, v. 2089). vistas, 'meeting', the formal meeting of king and vassal. quantos que y son, 'as many as are there' (y = there), as at v. 2060. partir se quieren, 'they wish to part', the pronoun between the infinitive and the verb governing it; partirse here 'to separate, withdraw', the leave-taking agreed for the next morning (v. 2112). que, 'for'. entrada era la noch, 'the night was come', the pluperfect of entrar made with ser.

sentences.t:
El rey a los ifantes a las manos les tomó,
metiólos en poder de mio Çid el Campeador:
sentences.l:
The king the Infantes by the hands them took,
put-them into power of my Çid the Campeador:
sentences.i: The king took the Infantes by the hand and placed them in the power of my Çid the Campeador:
sentences.n: Pidal's note: 'los tomó de la mano', 'took them by the hand'. a los ifantes … les: the Infantes named with a and taken up again by the pronoun. metiólos = metió + los, 'put them'. en poder de, 'into the power of': the formal handing over the king announced at v. 2101.

sentences.i: “Here are your sons, since they are your sons-in-law; from this day on, Campeador, it is for you to say what is to be done with them. Let them serve you as a father and honour you as their lord.”
sentences.n: Pidal's note: Evad aquí, 'he aquí', 'behold, here is' (compare evades aquí, v. 253). quando, 'since', causal. de oy mas, 'from today on' (mas = más, 'further'). sabed, imperative, 'know': 'see to it what to do with them'. fer = hacer. The third line is wholly in italics in the print: it is restored by Pidal, not the manuscript's, and no footnote here gives its source. It is printed without a number between 2124 and 2125; the letter b in 2124b is ours, as the house does with unnumbered restored lines. sírvanvos = sirvan + vos, present subjunctive as a wish, 'let them serve you'; the accent on the í is small on the scan and read as an accent. guárdenvos, 'let them respect you, keep faith with you' (guardar, 'to watch over, to observe'). cum = como, 'as'.

sentences.t:
—“Gradéscolo, rey, e prendo vuestro don;
Dios que está en çielo de[vos] dent buen galardon.
sentences.l:
—“I-thank-it, king, and I-take your gift;
God who is in heaven may-give-[you] for-it good reward.
sentences.i: “I thank you for it, King, and I accept your gift; may God who is in heaven give you a good reward for it.
sentences.n: gradéscolo = gradesco + lo, 'I am grateful for it'. prendo vuestro don, 'I take your gift': the Infantes, and the marriages. de[vos] = dé + vos, 'may he give you', the present subjunctive of dar printed without an accent; the vos is Pidal's (in italics). dent = de + ent, 'of it, for it' (= de ello). galardon, 'reward', printed without an accent. The Çid's speech does not close here: in Pidal's print the next line is v. 2131, which opens tirada 105 (a new assonance, á: natural, plaz; Pidal's rubric: El Cid no quiere entregar las hijas por sí mismo.—Minaya será representante del rey) and carries on the Çid's words to the king. The numbers jump from 2126 to 2131 because Pidal prints vv. 2127–2130 later, at the head of tirada 107 (after its rubric and before v. 2156), keeping their numbers; we follow his print order, and those four lines will come in their place there. Tirada 104 ends here.
